newsitem.title: USA: Thanksgiving dinner costs more this year.
newsitem.headline: Thanksgiving dinner costs more this year.

text.p: The cost of preparing Thanksgiving dinner for 10 people rose to more than $30 for the first time this year, a farm group said on Friday.

Higher-priced turkeys were the main culprit in lifting the cost of cooking the typical fare of turkey, stuffing, sweet potatoes, buttered rolls, peas, cranberries, cut-up carrots and celery, pumpkin pie, whipped cream, coffee and milk, the American Farm Bureau said.

Based on sample shopping excursions across the United States, the farm group estimated the average feast for 10 people will cost $2.02 more than last year at $31.66. It was the fifth consecutive year the cost of the meal has risen.
A 16-pound bird will cost shoppers 6 percent more than last year at $13.46.
The per-pound cost of turkey jumped six cents to 84 cents a pound, a rise attributed to strong consumer demand for turkey meat for sandwiches and other meals during the year.
Price increases were reported for 10 of 12 menu items, with a package of stuffing the only ingredient to cost less. By comparison the same meal cost $24.51 in 1987.
